#!/bin/sh
# Prikk uninstaller.
#
# Generated by `prikk-release-policy generate-installer` at release time and published as a
# release asset (never committed as a tracked .sh file) -- see docs/src/guide/install.md.
#
# Removes exactly what install.sh added: the binary at its install directory, the two licence files
# beside it (see the licence block below), and the marked PATH
# block install.sh may have appended to a shell startup file. Leaves everything else alone --
# nothing else Prikk creates (a repository's own .prikk directory, for example) is touched.
#
# Usage:
#   curl -fsSL https://github.com/REPO_SLUG/releases/latest/download/uninstall.sh | sh
#   curl -fsSL https://github.com/REPO_SLUG/releases/latest/download/uninstall.sh | sh -s -- --prefix /custom/path
#
# If you installed with a custom PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR, pass the same value here (either as --prefix or
# as the environment variable itself) so this script knows where to look:
#   PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR=/custom/path curl -fsSL .../uninstall.sh | sh
#
# Passing both at once is only accepted when they agree -- install.sh's own --prefix/--version pair
# never needs this check since each overrides only its own env-var default, but this script's one
# flag and the one env var name the same thing, so a disagreement between them would silently pick
# one and remove the wrong binary. 0.56.0 step U: found by an external consumer running
# `uninstall.sh --prefix <dir>` with no env var set and getting the default-location binary removed
# instead of the named one, because this script never read its own arguments at all until now.
#
# 0.56.0 step U2: a missing or empty --prefix value is refused here, by name, before --prefix is
# even recorded. Measured on the step-U template: `--prefix ""` set install_dir to the empty
# string, which made binary_path below resolve to "/prikk" -- a path nobody named -- and the script
# proceeded and printed "done" as if it had succeeded. A missing value (--prefix as the script's
# last argument) already aborted via `set -u`'s own "unbound variable" error when $2 did not exist,
# but with that raw shell message instead of this script's own. Checking `[ "$#" -lt 2 ]` first
# catches the missing-value case before $2 is ever referenced, so `set -u` never fires for it; `-z
# "$2"` catches the empty-value case. Both now refuse with this script's own message, exit 1,
# before anything is removed.

set -eu

install_dir=""
prefix_given=0

while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --prefix)
      if [ "$#" -lt 2 ] || [ -z "$2" ]; then
        echo "prikk-uninstall: --prefix needs a directory" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      install_dir="$2"
      prefix_given=1
      shift 2
      ;;
    *)
      echo "prikk-uninstall: unrecognized argument: $1" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$prefix_given" -eq 1 ]; then
  if [ -n "${PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR" != "$install_dir" ]; then
    echo "prikk-uninstall: --prefix $install_dir and \$PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR=$PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR disagree; pass only one" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
else
  install_dir="${PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
fi

binary_path="$install_dir/prikk"
path_marker_begin="# >>> prikk installer >>>"
path_marker_end="# <<< prikk installer <<<"

removed_binary=0
if [ -f "$binary_path" ]; then
  rm -f "$binary_path"
  removed_binary=1
  echo "prikk-uninstall: removed $binary_path"
else
  echo "prikk-uninstall: no binary found at $binary_path (nothing to remove there)"
fi

# 0.57.0 item 5b: the two licence files install.sh put under share/licenses/prikk, found the same way
# (a `bin` directory has its share/ beside it; any other directory holds its own), and nothing else
# in that directory. The directory itself goes only if it is then empty; the share/licenses above it
# is left, since other software may use it.
case "$(basename "$install_dir")" in
  bin) licence_dir="$(dirname "$install_dir")/share/licenses/prikk" ;;
  *) licence_dir="$install_dir/share/licenses/prikk" ;;
esac
removed_licences=0
for licence_file in LICENSE THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES; do
  if [ -f "$licence_dir/$licence_file" ]; then
    rm -f "$licence_dir/$licence_file"
    removed_licences=1
    echo "prikk-uninstall: removed $licence_dir/$licence_file"
  fi
done
if [ -d "$licence_dir" ]; then
  rmdir "$licence_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

removed_path_entry=0
for rc_file in "$HOME/.bashrc" "$HOME/.zshrc"; do
  if [ -f "$rc_file" ] && grep -qF "$path_marker_begin" "$rc_file" 2>/dev/null; then
    work_file="$(mktemp)"
    awk -v begin="$path_marker_begin" -v end="$path_marker_end" '
      $0 == begin { skipping = 1; next }
      $0 == end { skipping = 0; next }
      !skipping { print }
    ' "$rc_file" > "$work_file"
    mv "$work_file" "$rc_file"
    removed_path_entry=1
    echo "prikk-uninstall: removed the PATH entry from $rc_file"
  fi
done

if [ "$removed_binary" -eq 0 ] && [ "$removed_path_entry" -eq 0 ] && [ "$removed_licences" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "prikk-uninstall: found nothing to remove"
fi

echo "prikk-uninstall: done. Repositories under .prikk are untouched -- delete them yourself if you"
echo "prikk-uninstall: no longer want that history tracked."
